premise.claim: Issue #482: a Stateful RoleInstanceSet early rollback (A -> B -> A) tracks the replacement-in-progress signal in controller process memory (earlyRollbackReplacementSignals). After the stale base instance is deleted, a controller restart loses the signal; topology then treats the rollout as complete and condemns the existing surge while the replacement base is still unavailable, violating maxUnavailable=0.
premise.patchedComponent: same package + status.rolloutReplacementState API — exact match
premise.evidence: Reconcile-level fake-client repro on base main@ecdfd6e6 (results/premise-p0_base_repro_test.go, run from a detached worktree): post-restart state (in-memory signals empty, both revisions resolve to A, stale base deleted, healthy A surge at ordinal 1, replicas=1/maxSurge=1/maxUnavailable=0) — main deletes the surge (deleted=[p0-restart-1]) while the replacement base at ordinal 0 has only just been created and is unavailable. See results/premise-p0-base.txt. The same scenario on the PR head retains the surge (V1 canary).

findings.claim: After a restart, persisted rolloutReplacementState retains the surge while the replacement base is unavailable, recreates the base, and releases the surge + clears the state once the base is Ready (issue #482's expected behavior).
A changed target revision ends the recorded scope's surge protection (no stuck protection).

liveNote: No live cluster run for round 1: the defect is a controller-restart + informer-ordering race that the unit layer reproduces deterministically (in-memory signals empty == fresh process) and the envtest suite covers against a real API server (rollout_recovery_test.go seeds API-only state). The author additionally reports a delayed-watch A/B against a real API server (PR body, section V) — not re-run by the reviewer. The ACK live cluster is not needed for this premise.
